title: Fulfilment of Grant Obligations by International Students who Receive Study Grants
what_it_is: Fulfilment of Grant Obligations by International Students who Receive Study Grants

sections.label: MOE view on tuition grant bond
sections.summary: MOE takes a strong view of the tuition grant bond service commitment for international students.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: MOE takes a strong view of the tuition grant bond service commitment for international students.

sections.label: Tracking tuition grant bond compliance
sections.summary: Tracking shows more than eight in 10 graduates served or are serving bonds or have approved deferment, while a minority accounts for about $30 million of grants yearly.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Our tracking efforts show that for a typical batch of Tuition Grant recipients, the large majority – more than eight in 10 graduates – have served or are serving their bonds or have secured approval from MOE for deferment while they pursue further studies.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: However, there will inevitably be a minority for which our data cannot ascertain if they are fulfilling their service obligations.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: This minority group accounts for about $30 million of grants per year.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: This is around 2% of total grants to local students, or 1% of the budget spent on polytechnics and universities every year.

sections.label: Working or deferment rate
sections.summary: As of January 2016, 84% are working or have applied for deferment.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: As of January 2016, 84% are working or have applied for deferment.

sections.label: Consequences for defaulters
sections.summary: Defaulters face serious adverse consequences if they later apply to work or reside in Singapore, and the number of defaulters is falling.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: For example, where liquidated damages cannot be recovered, defaulters face serious adverse consequences if they subsequently apply to work or reside in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: This may be why the number of defaulters is falling and MOE will continue to monitor the effectiveness of these measures and improve them.

sections.label: Action against defaulting students
sections.summary: MOE recovers liquidated damages, failing which it will take serious, adverse actions against them.

sentences.speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat
sentences.text: So, has there been any action taken against such international students for not fulfilling their grants?

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: We recover liquidated damages, failing which we will take serious, adverse actions against them.
